questions.problem: Add: \(\dfrac{3}{x+2} + \dfrac{5}{x-1}\). Write as a single fraction.
questions.error_note: Kai set up the LCD correctly and distributed properly: \(3(x-1)+5(x+2) = 3x-3+5x+10\). But combined \(3x+5x\) as \(7x\) instead of \(8x\). The setup and distribution were perfect — just a mental math slip at the finish. Double-check coefficient addition on the final combine step.

questions.error_label: DIDN'T EXPAND f(x+h) — TREATED IT AS f(x)+h
questions.error_note: Kai computed \(f(x+h)\) as \(f(x)+h = 3x^2-2x+1+h\), then subtracted \(f(x)\) to get \(h\), divided by \(h\) to get \(1\). But \(f(x+h)\) means substitute \((x+h)\) for every \(x\): \(f(x+h)=3(x+h)^2-2(x+h)+1\). Expand: \(3(x^2+2xh+h^2)-2x-2h+1 = 3x^2+6xh+3h^2-2x-2h+1\). Subtract \(f(x)\): \(6xh+3h^2-2h\). Factor out \(h\): \(h(6x+3h-2)\). Divide by \(h\): \(6x+3h-2\).
questions.coaching_note: Same concept as Assessment 2A Q14. f(x+h) ≠ f(x)+h. Every x in the formula gets replaced by (x+h).
Same structure as Assessment 2A Q13 where Kai did term-by-term cancellation. This time: factored correctly as x(x+2)(x−2) / (x−2)(x+1), cancelled (x−2). Huge improvement.
